review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Nowadays, the news media have too much effect on people's life and this is not a positive development. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

On the one hand, admittedly, the widespread access to technology devices like smartphone or laptop and Internet. These technologies allow people to follow the news instantly whenever and wherever they are, so it naturally follows that the news becoming a regular part of their routine. Furthermore, the intense competition among lets, therefore, in order to gain attention, most media agencies that focus on shocking and breaking content moreover present it in a highly sensationalized manner with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visual. That can reinforce the overall impact of news on public opinion.

However, I strongly believe that have exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news. It is irrefutably true that when bad new is reported on varied social platform, people are constantly warned of existing and coming problems in the society. A piece of new on a tragic accident to illustrate in which a family of four all lost their live due to the father's driving under the influence of alcohol. If people are often exposed to this kind of new they are much more likely to avoid drunk driving.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that the proposal on this, it remain essential for public safety and awareness.

paragraphs: Some people argue that the news media have too much effect on people's lives and that this is not a positive development. Personally, I acknowledge this strong influence, although I am convinced that its effects are not entirely negative.

Admittedly, news media exert a considerable influence on people’s lives. One reason is widespread access to technological devices such as smartphones or laptops and to the Internet. These technologies allow people to follow the news instantly whenever and wherever they are; it naturally follows that the news becomes a regular part of their routine. Furthermore, the intense competition among news outlets means that, in order to gain attention, most media agencies focus on shocking and breaking content and present it in a highly sensationalized manner with dramatic headlines and an eye-catching visual. That can reinforce the overall impact of news on public opinion.

However, I strongly believe that news media have both harmful and beneficial effects. Exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news can overwhelm people, making them feel anxious and helpless. Nevertheless, it is irrefutably true that when bad news is reported on varied social platforms, people are constantly warned of existing and coming problems in the society. A piece of news on a tragic accident, in which a family of four all lost their lives due to the father's driving under the influence of alcohol, can illustrate this warning role. If people are often exposed to this kind of news, they are much more likely to avoid drunk driving.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that although news media have a considerable influence and can cause anxiety, they remain essential for public safety and awareness.
